messages:
maria: FYI we saw a ~12% drop in prefix cache hit rate after the kernel/latency patch rolled last night. Grafana alert fired at ~02:10 UTC. suspect surface: prompt normalization or a field ordering change in tool calls.
jon: ugh. saw the spike too. can you paste the cohort id? i want to run the hit-rate breakdown vs tokenizer version.
maria: cohort=stable-prod-2026-03, repro query attached below. quick diff of a sample request before/after:
```json
{
  "system": "You are a helpful assistant.",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize this doc"}],
  "tools": [{"name": "lookup", "args": {"id": 42}}]
}
```
anya: did we change how we stringify tool args? i remember a change to preserve insertion order in the tool serializer last week.
kevin: yes. PR #4122 uses ordered-dict serialization so callers get stable output. but that will change the literal bytes used for the prompt signature.
jon: that would explain a hit-rate drop if our cache key is naive. are we hashing the raw JSON blob or a normalized canonical form?
maria: currently we hash the post-processed request JSON (what goes into the tokenizer). no extra canonicalization beyond stripping trailing whitespace.
jon: ok that's fragile. propose: canonicalize tool args by sorting object keys except for a few whitelisted tool params where order matters (e.g., steps, route). also attach tokenizer-version to the key.
anya: +1 for tokenizer pin in key. i also want to add system prompt fingerprint separately so small edits to system message don't flush unrelated prefixes.
kevin: note: kernel selection fallback path inserts a small debug header into the prompt on certain devices, which could change the bytes and therefore the signature. maybe recent kernel rollout toggled that header for a subset.
infra-bot: [deploy-bot] Deployment 2026-03-17T23:58 -> kernel-v2.3.7 started on pool-gpu-4. No errors.
jon: thanks infra-bot. that matches the timeline. can we run a warmup backfill only for keys that lost hits? my idea: sample historical top-10k prefixes, regenerate canonical signatures under new rules, and re-populate the KV store with the mapped entries where possible.
maria: profiling note: when we re-encode sample 1k prefixes through the tokenizer pinned to v2 -> v3 we see tokenization length diffs in ~4% of cases due to new dropping of soft spaces. that affects cache alignment.
anya: then we should avoid relying solely on token-length for keying. better to use both (byte-hash + token-variant tag).
kevin: implementation detail: adding tokenizer version to the key is cheap, but we also need to update our metrics to slice hit-rate by token-variant to prove the hypothesis.
jon: i'll sketch a quick migration plan: (1) compute canonical_form(request) where canonical_form sorts tool object keys except whitelisted ones and normalizes system prompt by fingerprint; (2) key = sha256(tokenizer_version + '|' + canonical_form); (3) backfill top-N prefixes by mapping old-keys -> new-keys via a transform; (4) run canary warmup on 5% of traffic with automatic rollback.
maria: sounds good. two questions: how to handle function-call positional args that are order-sensitive? and will the backfill double-write cause racey overwrites?
anya: for position-sensitive args we add a @preserve_order flag in the canonicalizer metadata; that part of the object is left intact. backfill should write only if the destination key is empty or the TTL on KV is older-than threshold to avoid stomping fresher entries.
kevin: good guard. also suggest we run a mini A/B measuring latency impact of the canonicalizer (it adds CPU to request path). maybe offload canonicalization to an async worker for warmup-only path initially.
jon: agreed. i'll put up a draft RFC and a quick perf microbenchmark with 100k requests to get added CPU p50/p95 numbers.
maria: thanks. i'll open the incident ticket and tag ops to keep an eye on errors while canary is live. :thumbsup:
kevin: ping me when RFC is up, i'll review the serializer tests.
infra-bot: [alert] grafana: prefix-cache hitrate (stable-prod-2026-03) = 78% (baseline 89%). investigating.
jon: follow-ups: (a) RFC, (b) backfill script, (c) metric slices by token-variant + kernel-version, (d) small canary with async canonicalization. i'll own (a) and (b).
maria: assigning you. thanks everyone.
